prev: 25 Sep — Iran put its terms in public at the UN General Assembly: reopening Hormuz within seven days in exchange for released frozen funds, an end to sanctions and the lifting of the US naval blockade, conditional on restarting nuclear talks.
2–3 Nov — The US carried out what it called defensive strikes on Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz while mediators pushed a Hormuz deal; Hormuz stayed closed.

4–5 Nov — Iran called the US reply to its Hormuz plan "unconvincing" and set out seven conditions for reopening the strait; Trump confirmed the strikes. Mediated talks continue and the strait stays closed.
28 Oct–5 Nov — Russia agreed to resume three-way talks after US envoy Witkoff met Putin, yet launched a further missile barrage on Kyiv in early November.

10–11 Nov — Russia and Ukraine held their first direct, US-mediated talks in nine months in Abu Dhabi. They agreed a large prisoner exchange and Moscow's negotiator reported some progress, but there was no breakthrough, and Russia then fired about 22 missiles at Kyiv, killing six.
11 Nov — Headlines reported Tehran rejecting the US peace approach and vowing to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until Washington meets its conditions; mediated contacts continued.
12 Nov — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow, then Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin; the Kremlin said it was premature to call a peace deal close.

lead: The score is −49 today, unchanged from −49 at the last build and well down from −15 ten sessions ago; no indicator changed its reading today.
bullets: Nothing flipped, but the readings got worse. All 15 indicators kept the same bullish, neutral or bearish reading as at the last build, so the composite stays at −49. Under the surface the dollar index's 20-day rise grew to +1.89 points (was +1.29) and Bitcoin slipped to about $62,987 (today's daily candle is still part-way through).

Price is still fully bearish at −100. Bitcoin is 16.1% below its 350-day average (about $75,061), 13.4% below its 200-day average (about $72,699) and 19.0% below its 100-day average (about $77,776), all past the 5% bearish line (lagging, bearish). The 20-day high/low pattern is falling and none of the top-5 altcoins is above its 50-day average (coincident, bearish).

Liquidity is weak at −33. The market-implied chance of a Fed rate increase at the 10 Dec meeting is 98.1% against a 55% bearish line (leading, bearish), and the dollar index is up 1.89 points over 20 days against the +1.0 bearish line (leading, bearish). The one supportive reading is US government cash plus the Fed's reverse-repo balance, down $34.4bn over 20 days against a bullish line of down $25bn or more (leading, bullish), a much smaller drain than the $144.5bn at the last build.

Demand is −68 and weak. Bitcoin ETF net flows over the last 20 trading days are −$3,643m against a −$1,000m bearish line (was −$2,821m), and Ether ETF flows are −$1,356m against −$250m (coincident, bearish). Stablecoin supply is down 5.41% over 30 days against a −0.50% line (leading, bearish) and the 7-day vs 28-day ETF flow trend is −$69m against −$50m (leading, bearish). Bitcoin volume at 1.23 times its 30-day average against a 1.15 line is the one bullish reading (coincident), which in a falling market looks more like forced selling than new buying.

Positioning is +53 as leverage comes out. Funding is +0.009% per 8 hours, inside the +0.005% to +0.030% bullish band (leading, bullish). Bitcoin futures open interest is down 9.6% over 5 days while price is down 1.8%, so the bearish pattern of rising open interest into falling prices does not apply (leading, neutral). Liquidity is all leading indicators and price is all lagging ones, so when they disagree the composite understates liquidity's direction; here both are negative, so the composite of −49 is a fair summary.

moves.t: a close back above Bitcoin's 200-day average (about $72,699; $62,987 now, 13.4% below it) would move that indicator off bearish, and a recovery above the 100-day average (about $77,776) is needed to clear the third price indicator.
